entry.description: The compliance activity log of a Claude Enterprise organization (sign-ins, chats, projects and artifacts created, shared or deleted, members, API keys, settings), one log per activity, read from Anthropic's Compliance API.
entry.name: Claude Compliance
entry.setup:
1. The Compliance API needs a Claude Enterprise plan with the Compliance API enabled for the organization.
2. Create a key that can read compliance activities (`read:compliance_activities`): a Compliance Access key, or an
   Admin API key with that scope; copy it.
3. Each read is itself recorded as a compliance activity, so the log is read every five minutes.

streams.description: Every compliance activity as a log (source:claude-compliance-logs) with Anthropic's fields as they are; the tile's pipeline names the event (evt.name = type) and maps actor.email_address, user_id and ip_address to usr.* and network.client.ip.

A bucket is read once it has been closed for 15 minutes.

entry.description: The audit log of an Asana organization or workspace (logins, app authorizations, permission and privacy changes, exports, deletions), one log per event, read every few minutes from Asana's Audit Log API.
entry.name: Asana
entry.setup:
1. The Audit Log API needs an Enterprise or Enterprise+ plan.
2. In the Admin Console, open **Apps → Service accounts** and add one; copy its token (Asana shows it once). Give it
   the **Audit logs** scope when scopes are offered.
3. The workspace (domain) id is in the Admin Console's **Settings**, or in any project URL's first number.

streams.description: Every audit log event as a log (source:asana) with Asana's fields as they are; the tile's pipeline maps actor.* to usr.*, context.client_ip_address to network.client.ip and context.user_agent to http.useragent.

entry.description: The event log of a Bitwarden organization (logins, vault item, collection, group, member and policy changes), one log per event with the acting user, member and group resolved, read from Bitwarden's Public API (cloud US or EU, or a self-hosted server).
entry.name: Bitwarden

streams.description: Every organization event as a log (source:bitwarden): event is Bitwarden's record (type, device, ipAddress, actingUserId, memberId, groupId, itemId, collectionId, policyId, date); enrichment_details holds the acting user's, member's and group's names, emails and types read from the organization's members and groups.

entry.description: The enterprise events of a Box account (logins, uploads, downloads, shares, permission and user changes, Box Shield alerts), one log per event, read every few minutes from Box's Events API with a Client Credentials app.
entry.name: Box
entry.setup:
1. In the [Developer Console](https://app.box.com/developers/console), create a **Custom App** with **Server
   Authentication (Client Credentials Grant)**.
2. Under **Configuration**, set **App Access Level** to **App + Enterprise Access** and enable the application
   scope **Manage enterprise properties**; save.
3. Submit the app for authorization (**Authorization** tab); a Box admin approves it in the Admin Console
   (**Apps → Custom Apps Manager**).
4. Copy the client id and secret (**Configuration**) and the enterprise id (**General Settings**).

streams.description: Every enterprise event (admin_logs) as a log (source:box, service:enterprise-events) with Box's fields as they are; the tile's pipeline maps created_by to usr.*, ip_address to network.client.ip and the event type to its category.
streams.name: Enterprise events

entry.description: Cisco Duo's authentication log (results, factors, devices, applications), activity log, telephony usage, administrator actions and offline enrollments, one log per record, read from Duo's Admin API.
entry.name: Cisco Duo
entry.setup:
1. In the Duo Admin Panel, open **Applications → Protect an Application**, find **Admin API** and **Protect** it.
2. Under **Permissions**, keep only **Grant read log**; save.
3. Copy the integration key, the secret key and the API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`).

streams.description: Every authentication attempt as a log (service:authentication): result, reason, factor, user, application, access_device, auth_device, email.
streams.name: Authentication log

streams.description: Every activity record (admin and user actions, enrollments, policy changes) as a log (service:activity).
streams.name: Activity log

streams.description: Every SMS or phone call Duo sent, with its credits, as a log (service:telephony).
streams.name: Telephony log

streams.description: Every administrator action (logins, user, group, policy and application changes) as a log (service:administrator).
streams.name: Administrator log

streams.description: Every offline enrollment of Duo Authentication for Windows Logon as a log (service:offline_enrollment).
streams.name: Offline enrollment log

entry.description: The messages Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense judged scam, malicious, phishing, BEC, spam, graymail or neutral, with their verdicts, techniques and remediation, read from the Message Search API once their verdicts settle.
entry.name: Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense
entry.setup:
1. In Secure Email Threat Defense, open **Administration → API Clients** and copy the **API Key**.
2. **Add New Client**, name it (e.g. `observecraft`) and copy its client id and password.
3. Pick the API host of your region (the one your console's URL names).

streams.description: Every message with a verdict other than clean as a log (service:message): fromAddress, toAddresses, subject, verdict.latestVerdict / originalVerdict / techniques, action, urls, clientIP, direction. Windows are read 30 minutes after they close, so retrospective verdicts are in.
streams.name: Messages

dashboards.title: NetBird Overview
dashboards.description: Peers of a NetBird account (connected, last seen, expired logins, OS, client versions) and its audit log.

definition.content:
**NetBird** connects devices, servers and cloud resources over a WireGuard® overlay network. This dashboard shows the peers of the connected NetBird account (connected or not, last seen, expired logins, client versions) and its audit log: who added or removed peers, changed policies, routes, DNS and networks, created setup keys or invited users.

Connect an account in [Integrations → NetBird](/integrations/netbird): ObserveCraft reads its management API every minute, for NetBird Cloud and self-hosted NetBird alike.

definition.title: Peers added, removed and expired
definition.query: source:netbird @evt.name:(peer.user.add OR peer.setupkey.add OR user.peer.delete OR peer.login.expire OR peer.approve OR peer.approval.revoke)

definition.title: Access changes: policies, routes, networks, DNS
definition.query: source:netbird @netbird.category:(policy OR rule OR route OR network OR nameserver OR dns OR posture)

definition.title: Users, setup keys and tokens
definition.query: source:netbird @netbird.category:(user OR setupkey OR personal OR service OR account)
